summary: The Marshall Scholarship is a UK government scheme overseen by the Marshall Aid Commemoration Commission. Up to 50 awards are made in the 2027 competition to US citizens for one or two years of master's study, or up to three years including a PhD/DPhil, at a British university. It is open to US citizens only, so it is not available to other nationalities. It pays tuition fees, a monthly stipend, flights, visa and health-service costs and ambassadorial allowances.
eligibility_notes:
Candidates must be citizens of the United States at the time they apply. Permanent residents of the US are not eligible; a dual citizen who holds a US passport can apply.

They must hold a first undergraduate degree from an accredited four-year US college or university by the time the scholarship starts (September 2027). A degree from outside the US, for example Canada, does not qualify. The first undergraduate degree must have been completed after April 2024.

The undergraduate grade point average must be at least 3.7 on a 4.0 scale at the time of application. Rounded GPAs are not accepted. The most up-to-date undergraduate GPA is used and final transcripts are requested at interview stage. Only the GPA of the endorsing institution counts and graduate GPA does not count.

Candidates must not have studied for, or hold, a degree or degree-equivalent from a UK university, and must not have taken GCSE or A-level qualifications in the UK. A year abroad in Britain without receiving a degree is not a bar. Someone already enrolled at a British university is not eligible.

There is no age limit. A candidate applies for only one pathway, in only one region, and for either the one-year or the two-year scholarship, not both; applying for several leads to automatic disqualification. Applications must be endorsed by the President, Provost or Academic Dean of the applicant's US undergraduate institution (in exceptional cases the graduate school, with special permission). An endorsing institution may endorse no more than 24 applications. Candidates are asked to state whether they have applied for similar scholarships.
age_experience_notes: There is no age limit. The first undergraduate degree must have been completed after April 2024.
funding_summary: Awards cover tuition fees, a personal allowance (stipend) for accommodation and basic living costs, economy flights between the US and the UK at the start and end of tenure, UK visa fees and health charge, and extra allowances for ambassadorial activity. A one-year award lasts one academic year (10 to 12 months). A two-year award lasts two academic years. A PhD/DPhil started in year 1 carries third-year funding without a separate application, subject to progress. A third year for a PhD begun in year 2 is limited and decided by the Commission. Funding is never extended beyond a third year. The awards are not subject to UK income tax but may count as income for US tax.
programmes_note: Almost any subject at graduate level that leads to a British university degree. Not funded: second bachelor's degrees; postgraduate diplomas or certificates; degrees leading to professional qualifications in medicine, dentistry, veterinary science or law; courses giving a certificate of completion instead of a degree; distance-learning or largely online courses; part-time courses; supervised research with no degree; courses needing long periods away from the UK, including joint degrees with non-UK universities; MBA; MSc/MFE Financial Economics; courses starting in January or at any point other than the start of the academic year; master's courses longer than 12 or 24 months (including 15- or 28-month courses). Two-year candidates cannot use master's courses shorter than 9 months, and one-year candidates need a course of at least 10 months. The Oxford MPP is limited to one Marshall Scholar per year through a partnership with Brasenose College. The 1+1 combination of the Oxford MPP and MSc in Public Policy Research is not permitted. Candidates name first and second choice courses for each year of study. The Commission offers a course search tool.
institutions_note: Awards are tenable at any British university, and sometimes at other institutions offering degrees validated by a university. The Commission has partnership scholarships with a number of UK universities and welcomes applications to partner universities and to universities other than Oxford, Cambridge and London institutions. To be considered for a partnership award a candidate must list a partner university course as first choice for that year. Oxford and Cambridge applicants are not considered for partnership awards because those colleges are assigned by the Commission after selection. Candidates may not pick a first and a second choice in the same year from the group of Oxford, Cambridge, Imperial College London, King's College London, LSE and UCL. NIH Marshall Scholarships add extra funding years for biomedical PhDs at Oxford or Cambridge; those candidates must also apply separately to the NIH Graduate Partners Programme.

summary.detail: One-year master's (minimum 10 months, maximum 12), two consecutive one-year master's degrees, or one two-year master's degree. Full-time, in the UK, starting at the normal start of the academic year. Master's courses over 12 months (or over 24 months for a two-year course) are not funded.

A PhD/DPhil in year 1 (three years of funding guaranteed, subject to progress), or a one-year master's followed by a PhD/DPhil from year 2 (two years guaranteed; third year only at the Commission's discretion for strong academic reasons and subject to funds). Candidates should confirm they meet the PhD entry requirements and contact a possible supervisor before applying. Funding is not extended beyond three years.

benefits.conditions: Value varies with the course and location. Only for courses that follow the course rules (full-time degree courses at a UK university).

benefits.limit_text: Stipend of GBP 1,452 per month outside London and GBP 1,781 per month in London (2025-26 rate, given as an indicator)
benefits.conditions: Set by the UK Government and reviewed annually. Paid in quarterly instalments across the academic year; the first payment is made on arrival in the UK. Meant for accommodation and basic living costs. Military candidates who receive a salary get a reduced allowance. Other scholarships or income must be disclosed and the total of other funding cannot exceed GBP 10,000, for personal expenses only.

benefits.limit_text: Economy flights to and from the United States at the start and end of tenure
benefits.conditions: Fares cover economy air travel within the US from the home residence to the UK university (including travel to Washington DC for orientation if relevant). Return fares are paid after satisfactory completion of studies. Other travel costs are not met. Interview travel may be reimbursed for in-person interviews, up to an economy round-trip fare and unavoidable overnight stay, if the Commission's booking rules are followed. No reimbursement for virtual interviews.

benefits.limit_text: UK visa fees and the health surcharge that gives access to the National Health Service
benefits.conditions: Passport and other visa-related travel costs are not covered. The Commission takes no responsibility for other insurance against sickness, accident or death.

benefits.limit_text: Additional allowances to support ambassadorial engagement during the award
benefits.conditions: Amount not stated in the Rules.

benefits.limit_text: Dependants: no extra allowance for partners
benefits.conditions: The Commission may pay initial travel fares for dependants who receive dependant visas, a shipping allowance and a settling-in allowance, at its discretion and if agreed in advance. It does not cover dependants' visa costs.

requirements.text: Online application form, saved section by section and submitted to the undergraduate institution, which checks it and adds a letter of endorsement from the President, Provost or Academic Dean.

PDF copies of official academic transcripts from every university attended. Scanned or digital copies are accepted. Unofficial transcripts are not accepted and may make the application ineligible. Final transcripts are asked for again at interview stage.
Personal statement (maximum 750 words) on intellectual development and other interests.

Proposed academic programme (maximum 500 words): reasons for the chosen course and university, a brief reason for second choices, and for research degrees an outline research proposal and who the candidate would like to work with.
Leadership statement (maximum 500 words): a situation working with a group where the candidate saw and met a need for leadership.
Ambassador potential statement (maximum 500 words): how the candidate will act as an ambassador between US and UK communities and why the UK suits their interests.
Post-scholarship plan (maximum 350 words): immediate plans after the award, ongoing UK connections, and medium and long term career plans.
One-year scholarship statement (maximum 300 words): how the aims of the programme will be met within one year.
requirements.conditional_rule: Only for applicants for the one-year award.

requirements.text: Three letters of recommendation, each up to 1,000 words, uploaded as a PDF by the recommenders. The first recommender should have supervised the candidate's university training. The general letter must come from an academic; one letter should mainly address leadership and ambassadorial potential and need not be from an academic. At least two recommenders must be in the US. Recommenders need a secure link sent by the system.
Letter of endorsement from the candidate's US institution, added by the institution after it reviews the application.
Evidence of date of birth and US citizenship, such as a passport, with copies of original transcripts, given to the regional centre if invited to interview.
List of first and second choice UK courses and universities for each year of study, chosen within the course rules.

application_steps.title: Research courses and talk to your US institution early
application_steps.detail: Contact your undergraduate institution early. Read the Rules, check you meet the eligibility rules, choose a pathway and choose first and second choice UK courses for every year. You do not need a UK university offer before applying, but some UK courses (Oxford, Cambridge, Royal Academy of Music) close between October and early January.

application_steps.title: Complete the online form and statements
application_steps.detail: Apply in one region only and for one pathway. Fill in the online form, save each section, write the statements (word limits apply) and ask three recommenders through the system. No AI tools may be used to write the essays or answers; the institution must confirm the work is the candidate's own.

application_steps.title: Submit to your institution before the deadline
application_steps.detail: For the 2027 competition, applicants and recommenders had to submit by 5:00pm (time zone of the endorsing institution) on 29 September 2026; no changes after that. The institution then checks the application, adds the endorsement letter and submits it by 5:00pm on 1 October 2026. The institution may set an earlier internal deadline. Applications for 2028 are expected to open in summer 2027.

application_steps.title: Regional review and interview
application_steps.detail: Applications are reviewed at eight regional centres in the US. Shortlisted candidates hear by early to mid-November and are interviewed in November 2026 by a regional panel. Candidates abroad may interview virtually without penalty. Any part of the written application may be discussed at interview.

application_steps.title: Selection on three equal criteria and the offer
application_steps.detail: Selectors judge academic merit, leadership potential and ambassadorial potential; the course, university and pathway choices are also considered to widen the spread of universities and nations. The final selection is announced shortly after the interviews. Those selected are told in writing and must accept or decline in writing within 5 days. All awards depend on receiving an offer from a UK university.

application_steps.title: Confirmation letter and UK university applications
application_steps.detail: Scholars who accept receive a confirmation letter from the Commission in early to mid-December and must apply to their year 1 first-choice course if not already done. Oxford and Cambridge applicants should prepare but not submit until told the outcome; the Commission assigns the college. The Commission cannot guarantee admission. If a first choice is refused, the scholar applies to the second choice; changes to the choices after the offer are not considered.

application_steps.title: Visa, orientation, arrival and tenure rules
application_steps.detail: Scholars apply for UK entry clearance before arrival under special arrangements, with visa fees and health surcharge paid. Most travel to Washington DC for orientation and then to the UK as a group. Scholars study full-time and stay in the UK for the whole award, spend most vacations in the UK, and keep non-academic trips overseas to 30 days a year. Supervisors report yearly on progress and conduct. Year 1 must be completed before moving to year 2. Dismissal from the university ends the award.

notes: US citizens only: this scholarship is not available to other nationalities.
Applications for the 2027 competition are closed; dates quoted (29 September 2026, 1 October 2026, interviews in November 2026) are the 2027 cycle dates.
Stipend rates are the 2025-26 rates the Rules give as an indicator; they are reviewed each year.
